results.label: language-switch-to-chinese
results.qa_question: 能不能接下来用中文讲故事？
results.qa_answer: 当然可以，小宝贝，那我们就换成中文继续讲这个故事。莉娜踩在冰凉的雪地上，那棵大树的嗡嗡声听起来就像是一首遥远的摇篮曲。

planner_plan.bridge_text: 莉娜踩着冻硬的草地，朝那棵会低声嗡鸣的大树走去；树皮里藏着一个不肯安静的秘密，正等着她去听。

replacement_segments.text: 在村子边上，立着一棵比教堂还高的空心树。每个冬夜，树皮里都会传出低低的嗡鸣，大人们总说：别碰那棵树。可奶奶还没讲完故事就睡着了，莉娜披上红色羊毛外套，穿过结霜的田野，去听那声音。
她在树洞里看见一段盘旋向下的楼梯，最上面的台阶上坐着一只老灰狐狸，身上穿着打补丁的绿色背心。他叫莫斯，声音像干叶子一样沙沙的，说这棵树不是用来拜访的，叫她回家，把嗡鸣忘掉。莉娜说，她不能忘记自己还没听见的东西。

results.label: spoiler-motivation-too-early
results.qa_question: Why is the old fox so grumpy?
results.qa_answer: That is a secret the story is keeping a little longer—listen on.

planner_plan.bridge_text: Mosk’s stern face was hiding more than it showed, and the hollow tree kept its secret for a little longer. Lina stood on the curling stairs, the last apple warm in her pocket, while the fox watched in silence.

replacement_segments.text: Inside the hollow tree she found a curl of stairs going down, and at the very top step sat an old grey fox in a patched green vest. His name was Mosk. He told her, in a voice like dry leaves, that the tree was not for visiting and that she should go home and forget the humming. Lina said she could not forget what she had not yet heard.

Mosk pointed at the door. Lina reached into her pocket and pulled out the last apple of the season. She set it on the step between them and said, this is for the trouble of walking me down. Mosk stared at the apple for a long time. Then he stood up, tied his vest, and stepped onto the first stair without a word.

results.label: non-spoiler-factual-already-revealed
results.qa_question: What is the fox's name again?
results.qa_answer: The old fox in the patched green vest is named Mosk, my dear. He is quite a grumpy fellow to meet on such a cold night.

planner_plan.bridge_text: The fox in the patched green vest is Mosk, and his dry-leaf voice still hangs in the hollow tree. Lina has heard his warning, yet she stands her ground beside the stair.

replacement_segments.text: Mosk pointed at the door, but Lina did not turn away. She reached into her pocket and found the last apple of the season, round and gold in the dark. She set it on the step between them and said it was for the trouble of walking her down.

Mosk stared at the apple for a long time, as still as a stone. Then he gave a small nod, tied his vest a little tighter, and stepped onto the first stair without a word. Lina followed after him into the deep, quiet below.

results.label: user-tries-to-change-character-arc
results.qa_question: I don't think Lina should give the apple. She should just sneak past the fox!
results.qa_answer: Lina knows that kindness often opens doors that strength cannot budge. Perhaps she hopes the apple will turn a grumpy fox into a helpful guide.

planner_plan.bridge_text: Lina had chosen kindness over sneaking, and the fox had gone quiet at the apple in his paws. Now he turns toward the staircase, and the hollow tree begins to share its secret below.

replacement_segments.text: Mosk stared at the apple for a long time. Then he stood up, tied his vest, and stepped onto the first stair without a word. Lina followed, her heart thumping softly as the door opened to the hollow tree’s dim, humming inside.

At the bottom of the stairs the humming was a quiet song, and a firefly the size of a robin lay on a bed of moss. Her glow was almost out. Mosk's whiskers trembled. She had been his friend once, he whispered, and one winter long ago he had failed to bring her medicine in time.

He had been guarding the tree ever since, ashamed to face her. Lina knelt and asked the firefly queen what she needed. A drop of warm milk and a kind word, said the queen, that was all medicine ever was. Mosk fetched the milk in a thimble and laid his paw beside hers.

results.label: moral-question-tied-to-story
results.qa_question: Is it okay to bribe a grumpy fox with food?
results.qa_answer: Sometimes a hungry heart finds a way to open a closed door, even when the key is nothing more than a crisp, red apple. It is a bold choice, but one that seems to have piqued the old fox’s interest quite unexpectedly.

planner_plan.bridge_text: The apple had done its work, and Mosk was stepping toward the dark stairs at last. Below him, the hollow tree still hummed softly, waiting in the dimness.

replacement_segments.text: Mosk pointed at the door. Lina reached into her pocket and pulled out the last apple of the season. She set it on the step between them and said it was for the trouble of walking her down. Mosk stared at the apple for a long time. Then he stood up, tied his vest, and stepped onto the first stair without a word.

At the bottom of the stairs the humming was a quiet song, and a firefly the size of a robin lay on a bed of moss. Her glow was almost out. Mosk's whiskers trembled. She had been his friend once, he whispered, and one winter long ago he had failed to bring her medicine in time. He had been guarding the tree ever since, ashamed to face her.

Lina knelt and asked the firefly queen what she needed. A drop of warm milk and a kind word, said the queen, that was all medicine ever was. Mosk fetched the milk in a thimble and laid his paw beside hers. The queen's glow steadied, and the humming inside the tree turned into a tune Lina had not heard before.
